title: Inverse-Root Support, Polynomial Amplitudes, and Laurent Moment Channels
shortTitle: The combined support and moment atlas
oneLine: A combined unrefereed candidate extends the all-degree fixed-seed atlas to every polynomial amplitude, specified zero-cycles, all endpoint moments for q(P)≤3, and an exact Laurent local-channel criterion.
abstract: For a complex polynomial phase P, the fixed-seed cyclic rank equals both the nonzero residue support of the normalised inverse series at infinity and the reduced constant span of the generic inverse roots. Relative to named classifications of primitive polynomial monodromy and finite projective linear groups, the candidate classifies every phase with fixed-seed rank at most three and every proper rank-preserving polynomial extension. Version 0.7 then replaces dx by an arbitrary polynomial amplitude A(x)dx. If G'=A, the induced cyclic rank is the number of non-trace residue channels in G(ξ(t)), equivalently the reduced constant span of the values G(x_j); in particular, rank zero is exactly G∈C[P]. A specified zero-cycle vanishes exactly when its discrete Fourier transform annihilates every active channel. Combining the Pakovich–Muzychuk polynomial moment theorem with the low-rank right-factor list gives a complete persistent endpoint-moment classification for every Atlas phase q(P)≤3. For a Laurent phase L with zero-pole order m and local inverse L(φ(τ))=τ^{-m}, every Laurent one-form satisfies Res₀ L^k A dz=[τ^{mk-1}]A(φ(τ))φ'(τ). Known indecomposable Laurent examples rule out a composition-only global classification, so no finite all-Laurent atlas is claimed. Producer-side exact replay, mutation controls, partial Lean checks, deterministic rendering, and bounded literature audits support the package. They do not establish independent reproduction, complete formalisation, external specialist review, peer review, correctness of imported classifications, novelty, or priority.
narration: Start with a polynomial phase P and the exponential integral generated by one form, dx. Earlier versions showed that its cyclic rank can be read from the inverse of P at infinity: split the inverse series into congruence channels and count the nonzero ones. Relative to named monodromy and finite-group classifications, version zero point six used that bridge to classify every fixed-seed phase of rank at most three and every polynomial extension that preserves rank. Version zero point seven brings the theory into one combined paper and changes the seed. For any polynomial amplitude A dx, choose a primitive G with derivative A. The new theorem says that the induced rank is exactly the number of non-trace channels in G composed with the inverse branch. Rank zero occurs precisely when G is a polynomial in P. The same Fourier picture gives an exact test for vanishing on any specified zero-dimensional cycle. For ordinary endpoint moments, the candidate combines the established Pakovich–Muzychuk moment theorem with the Atlas right-factor list. This yields a family-by-family classification for every phase whose fixed-seed rank is at most three. Laurent phases require a different boundary. If a local inverse φ satisfies L of φ equals τ to the minus m, then every residue moment is one explicit coefficient of A of φ times φ prime. That criterion is exact for each specified Laurent phase and one-form, but it is not a finite classification of all Laurent pairs. The package passed producer-side replay, mutation, archive, document, and public Linux checks. It remains an unrefereed theorem candidate, not independent reproduction, complete formalisation, external specialist review, or priority certification. The scholarly creator is Anonymous. Operational maintenance and publication roles are recorded in the machine-readable provenance.

problem.name: Fixed-seed cyclicity and persistent moments for polynomial and Laurent phases

keyResults: For every complex polynomial P of degree at least two, the fixed-seed cyclic rank equals both the nonzero inverse-at-infinity residue-channel count and the reduced constant inverse-root-span dimension.

Relative to named primitive-polynomial-monodromy and finite-projective-group classifications, every phase of fixed-seed cyclic rank at most three and every proper rank-preserving polynomial outer extension belongs to the stated finite family list.
For every polynomial amplitude A dx with primitive G, q(P,A dx) equals the non-trace support of G(ξ(t)) and the reduced span of the values G(x_j); rank zero is equivalent to G belonging to C[P].
For a specified zero-cycle, persistent vanishing is equivalent to its discrete Fourier transform annihilating every active amplitude channel.
Combining the Pakovich–Muzychuk theorem with the complete low-rank right-factor list classifies persistent endpoint moments for every Atlas phase with q(P)≤3.
For every specified Laurent phase and Laurent one-form, all residue moments are governed exactly by the coefficients [τ^{mk-1}]A(φ(τ))φ'(τ); no finite all-Laurent normal-form atlas is claimed.

The degree-twenty atlas, preregistered degree-thirty-two experiment, bounded regressions, Lean controls and exact CAS checks remain producer-side support rather than substitutes for the written proofs or imported theorems.
evidence: A 25-page combined anonymous manuscript; a deterministic 338-file payload and 339-member archive; machine-readable combined claims and assurance records; exact global and amplitude/Laurent receipts; sixteen scoped Lean theorem controls and ten exact global CAS checks; ordinary-versus-optimised receipt parity; semantic mutation tests; exact Krylov-versus-inverse-support, zero-cycle, endpoint and Laurent direct-versus-local checks; preservation of the degree-twenty atlas and preregistered degree-thirty-two experiment; deterministic HTML/PDF rendering with static KaTeX, qpdf validation, a content-derived identifier and raw-TeX preflight; page-by-page visual QA of all 25 pages; clean-extraction replay; successful public GitHub Actions run 32516149843; immutable GitHub tag dba3a76df7bac00eb78331c6c2a1598248a822bb; and seven byte-identical GitHub and Zenodo assets. This establishes strong producer-side consistency, replay and availability, not independent theorem verification.
statusDetail: Public anonymous unrefereed theorem candidate. The all-degree fixed-seed classification and extension oracle remain relative to named primitive-polynomial-monodromy, composition-kernel and finite-projective-group inputs. The amplitude-support, rank-zero, specified-zero-cycle and Laurent local-channel arguments are written in the combined manuscript; the endpoint table additionally imports the peer-reviewed Pakovich–Muzychuk polynomial moment theorem and the unrefereed low-rank right-factor classification. Lean verifies selected fixed-seed consequences rather than the full function-field, monodromy, Kummer, Ritt, amplitude, endpoint or Laurent argument. No unaffiliated rerun or implementation, complete proof-assistant formalisation, identified external specialist sign-off, editorial peer review, settled novelty or priority determination, finite all-Laurent atlas, or demonstrated field impact is claimed.

decisionObject.description: A combined inverse-support, amplitude-channel, zero-cycle, endpoint-factor and Laurent local-channel calculus.
decisionObject.scope: All complex polynomial phases of fixed-seed rank at most three for the Atlas and endpoint table; arbitrary polynomial amplitudes and specified zero-cycles for a fixed polynomial phase; and the exact local coefficient test for each specified Laurent phase and Laurent one-form.
